newsitem.title: ERITREA: Rebels say they captured Sudan governor of Kurmuk.
newsitem.headline: Rebels say they captured Sudan governor of Kurmuk.

text.p: The rebel Sudan Peoples' Liberation Army (SPLA) said on Saturday the Sudanese governor of Kurmuk was one of the prisoners captured when the town fell to a rebel force last weekend.

Spokesman Yassir Arman told Reuters in the Eritrean capital of Asmara: "The governor of Kurmuk has been captured. He was among the prisoners-of-war taken when we captured Kurmuk on Sunday. His name is Hussein Yacob. He was captured with some of his aides."

SPLA forces, part of the opposition National Democratic Alliance, said they captured the town of Kurmuk on the Sudan-Ethiopia border last Sunday, January 12. Since then, they have claimed the capture of several Sudan army garrisons in the Southern Blue Nile area.
Arman said nothing about developments on the front on Saturday.
On Friday, the SPLA said the rebels would concentrate their efforts on the town of Damazin, which holds a hydro-electric plant that supplies Khartoum with most of its power.
Also on Friday, the rebels said they had seized control of the town of Maban. But the Sudan government rejected the claim.

Arman spoke on the Sudan reaction: "That is absolute rubbish. Our forces are in Maban. Either they (Sudan) are lying or they do not have command of their forces. We took Maban, and the government troops were fleeing toward Ulu and Muluth".

Northern and southern rebels working together in their first combined offensive to overthrow Khartoum's Islamist government say they are responsible for the attacks against army units in the east, which began earlier this week.
Sudanese rebels in Asmara and Cairo said a joint rebel force had captured Maban, which they said is a strategic bypass for the White Nile state, Upper Nile and the Blue Nile region.

Sudanese Information Minister and government spokesman Brigadier al-Tayeb Ibrahim Mohamed Khair denied the rebel claim, telling a news briefing in Khartoum that the situation in the Blue Nile area "is quiet with no movement on the enemy side".
Sudan says neighbouring Eritrea and Ethiopia are orchestrating the fighting but both countries, which host Sudanese rebels, reject the allegations.
The rebels say their objective is not to capture Khartoum but to strangle it and provoke an uprising against President Omar Hassan al-Bashir's Islamist military government.
Damazin is about 480-km (300-miles) southeast of Khartoum and supplies Khartoum with up to 80 percent of its power.
